public_rationale: DeepSeek and Ai2 report training estimates far below a billion dollars. These materially challenge a claim about the cost of a completed training run. They do not measure the same thing as a developer's total annual training or development expenditure. The passage shifts between those scopes and supplies no accounting basis for the general assertion, so the money-claim rules prevent a supported or contradicted verdict. The separate judgment about justified investment has no objective test.
limitations: Unknown accounting basis blocks a definitive money verdict.
The reported figures are rental-equivalent estimates with exclusions, not complete audited development costs.
A reading restricted to completed training runs would face strong contrary evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Once the financial mania recedes, current LLM uses will not be enough to justify further investment, and a true LLM cannot be trained on the cheap.

statement.excerpt: None of that is enough to justify further investment once the financial mania recedes. You cannot train a true Large Language Model on the cheap.

from_speaker: None of that is enough to justify further investment
You cannot train a true Large Language Model on the cheap
You are always spending billions of dollars
our_interpretation: The checkable component is the asserted necessity of billion-dollar spending to train a genuine large general-purpose language model.
The surrounding phrase always spending billions supplies the ordinary meaning of not cheap. A comparable cost below USD 1 billion would be a clear counterexample.
This is assessed as a claimed technical resource requirement, rather than a company's results for a particular reporting period.
The passage moves between training an individual model and OpenAI's aggregate annual training expenses. It does not establish a common accounting basis or cost boundary.
The post-mania investment sentence is evaluative and has no stated return threshold; it cannot be settled merely by observing that someone invests.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable and sufficiently comprehensive cost evidence establishes that training the relevant class of LLM requires billion-dollar expenditure, rather than merely showing that some developers choose to spend that much.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented genuine LLM is trained for less than USD 1 billion on a cost basis matching the claimed requirement, including any prerequisite training costs included in that requirement.

evidence.locator: Section 1, paragraph discussing Table 1 training costs
evidence.explanation: This is substantial evidence against a billion-dollar minimum for a completed training run. The report prices GPU hours at an assumed rental rate and excludes prior research and ablation experiments, so it is not a comparable all-in company expenditure figure.

evidence.excerpt: At a price of $2/H100 hour, this would cost $2.75M.
evidence.explanation: The report estimates the GPU-rental-equivalent cost of applying its developed recipe to Olmo 3 Think 32B. It excludes substantial research changes and does not provide an all-in financial accounting, so it challenges the per-run reading without settling the broader expenditure claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Specify the relevant model class and cost boundary, then obtain comparable costs including all required components. One qualifying model below USD 1 billion would refute a matching universal minimum-cost claim.
